title: A Comprehensive Study of Automatic Program Repair on the QuixBugs Benchmark
role: empirical counterevidence for test-suite-passing versus semantically correct patches; narrows novelty
evidence_note: Reports 53.3% of 338 plausible QuixBugs patches manually assessed as overfitting. The result is benchmark/tool-specific, and automated detector accuracy varies substantially by technique; it is not a universal overfitting rate.

title: Empirical Review of Java Program Repair Tools: A Large-Scale Experiment on 2,141 Bugs and 23,551 Repair Attempts
role: counterevidence that repairability is benchmark-dependent; narrows generalization claims
evidence_note: Eleven Java repair tools were tested on five benchmarks. The paper reports patches for 21% of bugs overall, 47% on Defects4J and 10–30% on other benchmarks. The cohort is Java/test-suite-based and does not give a universal rate for all repair systems.

title: Automated Patch Assessment for Program Repair at Scale
role: follow-up validating assessment difficulty while documenting assessment-oracle failure modes
evidence_note: Finds 10 of 97 semantically-equivalent-to-human patches previously claimed correct were overfitting, but also reports false positives when generated tests violate implicit input preconditions. Human reference patches are not perfect oracles; automated assessment improves scale but does not remove oracle judgment.

title: Coupled Requirements-driven Testing of CPS: From Simulation To Reality
role: adjacent-domain counterevidence on simulation-to-field assurance; not direct medical-device evidence
sections_checked: abstract claims about simulation fidelity and coverage
evidence_note: Proposes an initial framework for sUAS and robotic CPS testing across simulation, hardware-in-the-loop, and field contexts. It highlights fidelity, scenario coverage, and traceability gaps, but calls results preliminary and does not establish these findings for medical devices.
